standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic breaking down projects task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: A worked example walks through organizing a bedroom closet by Saturday: put everything back, wipe the empty shelves, sort into keep, donate, and toss, then pull everything out onto the floor first, read in that order from the deadline backward.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g8-u01-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g8-u01-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g8-u01-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g8-u01-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Did working backward from the deadline change any step you would have otherwise forgotten or left too late? Name it.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u01-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u01-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u01-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Backward-planning technique: The last step is written first and at least four steps are correctly sequenced backward to a genuine first action. | Time estimation reasoning: Each step has a distinct, realistic time estimate. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u01-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner apply the same backward technique to a second, unrelated real project and compare: did the number of steps or the hardest-to-predict step change between the two projects?

resources.title: breaking down projects worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: A worked example walks through organizing a bedroom closet by Saturday: put everything back, wipe the empty shelves, sort into keep, donate, and toss, then pull everything out onto the floor first, read in that order from the deadline backward.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact breaking down projects decision or action.
Model move 2: Study this worked example once before writing anything.
Model move 3: Choose one real project of your own with a real or realistic deadline, a school assignment, a room to organize, or preparing for a specific event.

Model check: Backward-planning technique: The last step is written first and at least four steps are correctly sequenced backward to a genuine first action. | Time estimation reasoning: Each step has a distinct, realistic time estimate.

resources.title: breaking down projects action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for breaking down projects.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: breaking down projects coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: A worked example walks through organizing a bedroom closet by Saturday: put everything back, wipe the empty shelves, sort into keep, donate, and toss, then pull everything out onto the floor first, read in that order from the deadline backward.
Coach direction: Study this worked example once before writing anything.
Learner prompt: In your own words, explain why starting from the deadline and working backward is different from just listing steps in the order you'd normally think of them.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: breaking down projects complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Choose one real project of your own with a real or realistic deadline, a school assignment, a room to organize, or preparing for a specific event. Using the same backward technique as the model, write your last step first, then work backward through at least four steps to your very first action.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I wrote my last step, what 'done' looks like, first.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I worked backward through at least four steps to my very first action.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: breaking down projects minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Did working backward from the deadline change any step you would have otherwise forgotten or left too late? Name it.

Success checks: Backward-planning technique: The last step is written first and at least four steps are correctly sequenced backward to a genuine first action. | Time estimation reasoning: Each step has a distinct, realistic time estimate.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: breaking down projects supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g8-u01-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g8-u01-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional breaking down projects condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Backward-planning technique: The last step is written first and at least four steps are correctly sequenced backward to a genuine first action. | Time estimation reasoning: Each step has a distinct, realistic time estimate..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u01-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: breaking down projects — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the breaking down projects task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Did working backward from the deadline change any step you would have otherwise forgotten or left too late? Name it.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u01-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u01-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u01-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Backward-planning technique: The last step is written first and at least four steps are correctly sequenced backward to a genuine first action. | Time estimation reasoning: Each step has a distinct, realistic time estimate.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u01-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
